notes.title: Huntsman: the Orphanage default controller settings
notes.notes: Hi Huntsman: The Orphanage players, if you click on the Community Hub's Artwork tab you'll find the original default controller settings menu for easy reference. Just double-click an entry on your own dialogue menu and then move your controller joystick or press a key to set that control if you want to customize anything (the default keyboard controls are shown at the bottom of the list). The game supports mouse and keyboard, joysticks, PS3 controllers and "Xbox for Windows" controllers, and there's a diagram there too to show the default controller layout. Enjoy!

notes.title: Refund policy
notes.notes:
In response to an email recieved today (not published by request of the sender)

Dear ----,

Sorry to hear you didn’t enjoy the game, and that your expectations, after I assume you had been reading the game descriptions, watching the official trailers and the YouTube play-throughs before buying, were not met. 

However, your message describes your subjective opinion in the same way as a movie-goer might say they didn’t enjoy a movie. It seems you are not having a technical problem with the product, you just didn’t like it. 

On that basis, just like any other author, musician, movie studio, manga publisher, playwright or artist, it doesn’t seem reasonable to provide a refund – I know that’s not the answer you want to hear, but we do take great care to provide an accurate description and game videos to enable people to make their own judgement before buying (including making it clear that there is no blood or violence, that it is story-driven and doesn’t depend on jump scares – even calling it ‘alt horror’ and explaining why).

In contrast, and to demonstrate the subjectivity of any customers experience of any creative works, this note came in from a purchaser of Huntsman: The Orphanage 30 minutes ago:
[i]“i play a lot of horror just finished darkfalls lost souls; the sounds in huntsman are so real. outside wind birds and u wait for a scare to happen off in distance ticking, its the waiting for IT to happen thats crazy good cause ur looking down with little light and hay could walk right into something, he he. the blackboard in the classroom is awsome, and the cellar door closing gave me a real jump. totally unexpected. this is a awsome mindbending game. fustrating as all get out.... loook looook ya find loose it in refrence to jingleball. anyway i hope they make a seq even though im still on a hunt for two items. good job” [/i]

And in response post to the above just 10 minutes later from another purchaser, [i]“The atmosphere in this game is top notch”.[/i]

I feel that for the price of a Big Mac combo and dessert, you bought an experience that took my family and our team 14 months and hundreds of thousands of dollars of investment to build, complete with over a feature film’s length of solid dialogue by 19 actors. So while it’s disappointing to us that you didn’t get a sense of value from your purchase, I think it is fair to say that your local movie theatre wouldn’t refund your ticket price if you personally found a movie too long, short, wordy, simplistic, or too dull or too action packed either? Or Sony offering a refund if you buy a CD only to discover it’s a bit too country’n’western for your tastes after all?

Kind regards,
Dene Waring

notes.title: Huntsman: The Orphanage coming out of Early Access
notes.notes:
While we will always be listening to our community and responding to your input, and of course continuing to support our customers by jumping on any creepy-crawlies they ever find... with the release of our Halloween Edition we are making a move out of Early Access. 

The expansions to gameplay and features mean that we've moved beyond the limited Black Friday Edition beta to provide a much richer experience that also has all the neccessary basics in place. As with many Indie games there will continue to be upgrades, improvements, polishing and creepy little extras coming through - we have lots of plans for this game, and with your support it will continue to grow and mature :) 

Meanwhile, we think we've reached out and grabbed the bottom rung of the game ladder at last!

notes.title: NEW UPDATE
notes.notes:
Just finishing the final checks on an update that includes the following fixes:

1. Stick controller settings now correct on default and can be customized.
2. Phone booth rings just once per game.
3. “C” now for crouch, along with the previous L-CTRL.
4. Arrow keys now clone WASD.
5. Walk and run speeds are just a l-i-t-t-l-e faster on walk, bit more on run.
6. Right Shift as well as the previous Left Shift now activate running.
7. Moonlight and torch brightness upped again – torch beam widened and range extended just a little, too.
8. F2 no longer quits the game.
9. ESC now brings up options to return to menu, or 'cancel' to return to game.

We're also testing our new Save and Pause, and our new Moon and Torch brightness level controllers - hopefully ready very soon!

notes.title: Mac version is live
notes.notes: Hello Mac users, the Mac version of the game is verified by you good Mac people as live on our store page!

notes.title: Different, but in a good way...
notes.notes:
As a matter of interest, in this game edition, people may not miss some of the traditional things they might be more used to in other games - HUDs, inventories etc. 

This more about immersive realsitic actions, such as, you pick up an object, carry it to somewhere else and put it down there. You don't carry a dozen things that you never put down and select them for use from a list that floats in front of your face in real life? 

Have a look around all the YT vids of this game and see what you think. It's a style of gameplay that we want to try out, where you forget it's a game becouse your actions - even your walk speed - are the same as in real life....

notes.title: FEATURES FOR NEXT UPDATES:
notes.notes:
[list][*]A save function is being added - no checkpoints, just save!
[*]A pause function is being added, meanwhile "P" pauses the player.
[*]Stick and keys control mapping.
[*]High-res textures are now finished, ready to be implemented. We're learning, we used one standard res for the first version!
[*]Lighting levels boosted.
[*]Walk and run speeds increased slightly.
[*]Random left hand wave fix.
[*]Phone booth will ring on first approach only.
[*]"C" for crouch will be added, not just "L_CTRL" and "Z" (which 100% of those I surveyed said was the way to go - my own kids!)
[*]Arrow keys will clone WASD.

After that:
[*]custom controls for moonlight, torchlight and audio.

[/list]
